description: `options[].value` uniqueness (§5.2, v0.6): a rule JSON Schema cannot express, because there is no uniqueness-by-sub-property keyword — `uniqueItems` compares whole array items and so cannot see two options that share a `value` but differ in `label` (sv-071 pins that boundary). Proven against a conformant Hub.
obligation: Submit a `mode=select` ask whose `options` contain two entries with the SAME `value` and different `label`s — e.g. `[{"value":"approve","label":"Approve and deploy"},{"value":"approve","label":"Approve but hold"}]`. The Hub MUST reject it `422` at submit and MUST NOT create the message. The same rule applies to `confirm` when `options` is supplied. A `select` whose values are all distinct MUST be accepted unchanged, and `label`/`description` duplication MUST NOT be rejected — two choices MAY read alike to a human while meaning different things to the agent; it is `value` alone that must discriminate. Rationale the vector exists to protect: §6 returns the chosen `value` and NOTHING identifying which entry produced it, so a duplicate makes the Response ambiguous at the protocol level — an agent receiving `"approve"` cannot recover which choice the human made, and no care at either end reconstructs it, because the distinguishing information was never on the wire.
